subject: botany
question_text: What constituents of DNA are linked by a glycosidic bond?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, Chapter 10 Biomolecules, book p.26, VSAQ 4. The book's answer — 'glycosidic bond is present between deoxyribose sugar and nitrogenous bases of nucleotides in DNA' — is CORRECT and is followed. This card adds the standard NCERT detail the book omits: the linkage is an N-glycosidic linkage, and the sugar-to-phosphate link is a separate phosphodiester bond. That second sentence corrects a common student error, not the book. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two constituents
lines: In DNA the glycosidic bond links
This sugar plus base unit is a nucleoside.
steps.why: A nucleotide has three parts — sugar, base and phosphate. The glycosidic bond joins only two of them, the sugar and the base, and the unit it makes is a nucleoside.
common_mistakes: Answering 'sugar and phosphate'. That link is a phosphodiester bond, not a glycosidic bond.
Answering 'base and phosphate'. The base is never joined to the phosphate.
steps.memory_tip: Sugar plus base is a nucleoside, and the glycosidic bond is what makes it.
steps.margin_note: Both names must appear: deoxyribose sugar AND nitrogenous base.

steps.label: The bond named correctly

lines.text: N-glycosidic bond: sugar C-1  ↔  base N-9 or N-1

lines: It joins carbon 1 of deoxyribose to
nitrogen 9 of a purine (adenine, guanine) or
The sugar and the phosphate are joined by a
phosphodiester bond, not by this bond.
steps.why: The link is called N-glycosidic because it reaches a nitrogen atom of the base. Naming the two bonds apart is what stops the mix-up with the sugar-phosphate backbone.
common_mistakes: Writing that the glycosidic bond forms the sugar-phosphate backbone. The backbone is held by phosphodiester bonds.
Writing 'hydrogen bond'. Hydrogen bonds hold the two strands together, not the sugar to the base.
steps.memory_tip: Glycosidic goes across the rung; phosphodiester goes down the backbone.
steps.margin_note: Two marks for a one-line question — add the N-glycosidic name and the contrast with the phosphodiester bond.

insider_note: Many answers say 'sugar and phosphate' from memory of the backbone. The glycosidic bond is sugar to BASE.
